value: An App Service feature for outbound calls to specific `TCP` endpoints, on-premises or anywhere that allows outbound traffic to Azure on port 443.
reason: Port 443 is the outbound path to Azure that the endpoint's network must allow, not a port the endpoint itself must listen on.

value: Integration never grants inbound private access to the app, so an app that must also be reached privately needs a private endpoint for that direction.
reason: The cached docs don't say the two are used together on one app; the new line says why each direction needs its own feature.

value: The overview makes an exception to scaling to zero: most apps can, but apps that scale on processor or memory load can't.
reason: 'Only' overstates: the docs also name Flexible profiles and Dapr actors as cases that can't scale to zero.

value: A and C keep both apps in one environment; the docs advise separate environments for apps that must never share compute, and for test versus production. D is an ACI construct, not Container Apps.
reason: Separate Dedicated workload profiles also avoid shared compute, so C needs the docs' own criterion to be clearly wrong.

value: The combinations run from 0.25 vCPU with 0.5Gi up to 4.0 vCPU with 8.0Gi, but a Consumption only environment caps apps at 2 cores and 4Gi.
reason: Adds the docs' note that Consumption only environments stop at 2 cores and 4Gi, so the range isn't read as open to every app.

value: A is the default maximum, not a fixed count. C would need a minimum of 1. D: the source says such an app scales to zero, not that deployment fails.
reason: The source doesn't say the app 'deploys'; it says the app scales to zero.

value: The custom IP address range, of public or private addresses, you specify when creating the virtual network; its resources get private addresses from it.
reason: The source says the space can use public and private (RFC 1918) addresses, not private ones only.

value: A ignores the overlap. C: a /20 holds 4,096 addresses, and even a /29 subnet is supported. D: 10.0.0.0/8 is a recommended private range.
reason: The old rebuttal of C spoke of subnets while the option is about the network's size.

value: The docs rule out a `CNAME` at the root domain, citing an internet standard for domain names, so the root maps straight to the app's IP address with an `A` record.
reason: The old line only said a standard is cited, without saying what the `A` record does instead.
